W3 (cost lens), after E009. The tip is E008: Muon, Lookahead/EMA and resizing 24/28/32 at 40/30/30%. It runs 9.5 epochs (HYP) at batch 2000, about 238 steps, and scores 6.98 s at 0.7572.

What was measured:
- E003/E004: compile plus fused SGD saved 14%. A recompile leak cost +3 s, so any new shape or graph carries leak risk.
- E005: EMA gave +0.97 pp at almost no cost.
- E006: Muon gave +0.66 pp for +4% time.
- E007: resizing saved 22% of time and cost 0.59 pp.
- E008: cutting 0.5 epoch saved 0.35 s and cost 0.18 pp, about 2 s per pp at the margin.
- E009: LR decay to 0 on top of EMA gave −0.08 pp, which is noise. EMA already fills the low-LR role, so H1.3.4 is refuted. E009 ran at the tip's 9.5 epochs (time 6.99), not at 10. My time miss there came from mislabeling the epochs.

Budget model: time ≈ F + V × pixel fraction.
- From E007→E008, about 0.7 s per epoch, so V(9.5 epochs) ≈ 6.65 s at a pixel fraction of 0.755. That gives about 8.8 s full-res-equivalent and F ≈ 0.3-0.8 s.
- Small resolutions use the GPU less efficiently, so I discount the predicted saving at ≤20 px by about 30%.
- Prices per unit of accuracy:
  - Resizing: about 3.5 s per pp so far, likely worse below 24 px and with a shorter 32-px tail.
  - Epochs: about 2 s per pp.
  - Width 576→512: about 5.5% fewer FLOPs, so about 4% of wall time. CIFAR-100 likely loses 0.2-0.4 pp, which is a bad price at this margin.

Systems: each step is about 25 ms of GPU-saturated work at batch 2000. Launch and Python overhead is probably ≤3-4% even under the 4-CPU pin. Overhead candidates:
- Muon's per-parameter loop: compiled, about 9 tensors.
- Lookahead foreach ops every 5 steps.
- The augment mask loop: 25 masked copies per epoch.

CUDA graphs might save 2-4%, with real risk of breakage (Python-float LRs in fused SGD, mutating state) or leaks.

Margin: 0.7572 − 0.753 = 0.42 pp at 3 seeds. Against a safety bar near 0.756 for the 40-seed judgment, the margin is about 0.1 pp. Every pure time cut that costs ≥0.3 pp falls below the bar. The remaining open levers are:
- accuracy-adding near-free changes: LS, wd or LR retune; BN recalibration;
- pure systems savings: the augment loop, the H2D/pad/whitening fixed cost;
- spending accuracy gained elsewhere on epochs.

Noise:
- Compiled runs are deterministic per seed. E003 and E004 gave identical accuracy, which supports H4.1.1.
- Per-seed std is about 0.2-0.35 pp, so the 3-seed SE is about 0.15-0.2 pp.
- Time noise is about 1-2%.

Unsure about:
- whether ≤20 px is super-linearly harmful;
- the offset between seeds 0-2 and the 40-seed mean;
- the true launch-overhead fraction under the 4-CPU pin;
- whether width or LS retunes are free.

forecasts.reason: The pixel fraction falls from 0.755 to 0.639, saving about 0.7 s after the efficiency discount. But 20 px plus a 20% 32-px tail should cost 0.4-0.8 pp, dropping below 0.753.
About 5.5% fewer FLOPs gives only about 3.5% wall-time saving, and CIFAR-100 likely loses about 0.25 pp. That buys too little time for too much margin.
The recipe is unchanged and seeds 0-2 are deterministic, so the task metrics should repeat E008. Event syncs add a little time. The held-out seed statistics will probably land within 0.3 pp.
Steps are GPU-saturated at batch 2000, so I expect a 1-3% saving, near the 3% threshold. There is a risk of baked LRs or leaks.

cruxes: How far is the 40-seed mean from the seeds 0-2 mean (I013)? It sets whether the real margin is 0.4 pp or about 0.1 pp, and so whether any accuracy-costing time cut is allowed.
Is there a near-free accuracy gain (LS 0.2 vs 0.3, wd/lr retune, BN recalibration) of ≥0.3 pp that could be spent on about 0.5-0.75 fewer epochs?
What fraction of the about 29 ms per step is launch or Python overhead versus GPU compute under the 4-CPU pin? This decides whether CUDA graphs and the augment-loop cleanup are worth anything.
